question: Can observables already accessible to KEP distinguish audit-backlog from deteriorating source correctness well enough to choose a useful lab-only verification strategy?

motivation.observer_note: Audit-age is a telemetry status, NOT proof source claims are right.

frozen_protocol.fallback_decision: If completed review age <=8h, use conservative. If older AND >=18 eligible paired observations during last 12h AND pair disagreement <= 0.35, use fixed_voi; otherwise conservative.
frozen_protocol.audit_age_only_control: If completed review age >8h, use fixed_voi; otherwise conservative.

design_warnings: AuditFeedback includes simulated true labels, but policy-visible ObservedVote and ReviewPulse MUST NOT include truth or future outcomes
Observational availability of a raw synthetic source vote at observed_at is an invented simplifying assumption, not external data proof
False or agreeing publisher roots can still be dependent; correlated rumor regime must be included even if it worsens performance
If source-degraded and stable worlds have equal telemetry, using audit-age alone cannot identify correctness
Only authored simulators and preselected comparators are measured. A passed threshold is not evidence of real provider performance
No policy or candidate module merges to main unless the experiment is GO and separately reviewed; NO_GO retains only report/protocol
test_value_rule: New tests only for observable time/label leakage, duplicate pair control, and preregistered refusal; avoid duplicating 880 prior tests.
